event.description: Reduce feed-forward width from retained 20 to 19 while retaining rank-3 learned positional factorization and the 45000-step learning-rate-floor schedule.
event.proposal: Family: feed-forward width. Retained incumbent is 3185 parameters at 99.990000%, a +0.990000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the current ff=20 setting was last accepted within the original width sweep at attempt-0003 (4288, 99.91%); the most recent failed result is attempt-0022's ff=19 micro-trial, an optimization failure with 9.9% peak validation under the earlier rank-8, 30000-step zero-ending setting; 4 prior family macro-attempts. The immediately preceding rank-2 positional attempt-0030 is an optimization failure (45000 steps, 11.1% peak validation, no checkpoint), not a scored nonqualification. Hypothesis: ff=19 may retain enough nonlinear capacity in the materially changed rank-3 positional representation and 45000-step nonzero-tail schedule, saving 56 actual parameters (3185 to 3129). This is parameterization-preserving feed-forward-width compression, not a representational substitution. It is more informative than the nearest untested ff=18 alternative because it isolates the one-channel boundary from a high-margin incumbent before any larger bottleneck reduction.
